bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang ousted — leadership vacuum, export scandal, ecosystem funding at risk
bullets.body: Jensen Huang was pushed out as NVIDIA CEO following reports of illicit chip sales to China via third-country pass-throughs and a personal relationship scandal; Colette Kress named interim CEO. The stock fell 14% intraday before recovering to -4.3%, erasing ~$600B in market cap, with 10% of float trading hands WTD. Core investor concern: Kress is expected to curtail Huang's aggressive ecosystem financing (the $500B August backstop made zero deals), threatening neocloud funding — NBIS -17%, CRWV -7% on the news. AMD +6%, AVGO +5.5%, ANET +5% traded as beneficiaries on custom-chip share gain expectations.

bullets.title: NVDA export control scandal deepens — MATCH Act acceleration, DOJ antitrust probe, 240K chips diverted to China
bullets.body: DOJ opened a direct antitrust probe into NVIDIA and separate investigations into SMCI and Megaspeed (linked to Alice Huang), while reports show ~240,000 NVDA AI chips were diverted to China via Singapore-based Aperia Cloud Services and China-controlled SEA neoclouds. The DoC is finalizing rules blocking Chinese firms from remote access to advanced AI chips across seven SEA countries. The MATCH Act, which would harmonize export controls with Japan and the Netherlands, may be accelerated by the Democrat-controlled Congress, and Jensen Huang is expected to testify before the Senate Banking Committee in December.

bullets.title: Fed tightening cycle extending — BofA adds Jan '27 hike, terminal rate now 4.5-4.75%; Williams hawkish
bullets.body: BofA added a 25bp hike in January 2027 to its Fed forecast, now expecting hikes at December, January, and March meetings, pushing the terminal rate to 4.5-4.75%. Fed's Williams reiterated inflation remains too high and further tightening is needed. PPI data and Fed speakers (Goolsbee, Collins, Logan, Bowman, Daly, Jefferson) are on the schedule for today.

bullets.title: Rates/yields surging — 10Y at 5.12-5.15%, 30Y mortgage 7.42%; upside inflation risk flagged as 'very real'
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 14bps to 5.12% Thursday and is up another 3bps to 5.15% in premarket Friday. 22V Research flags upside inflation risk as 'VERY real' over coming months, citing AI-driven demand lifting normally disinflationary electronics prices and CEO cost pass-throughs accelerating. Their short-term call is paradoxically long risk/short VIX, arguing most investors underestimate inflation, while their longer-term pivot back to bullish risk assets requires dovish core PCE (≤21bps/month).

bullets.title: Existing home sales hit 16-year low; mortgage rates at 7.42% — real estate sector under pressure
bullets.body: Existing home sales fell to 3.75M SAAR (-5.5% m/m, -8.8% y/y), the lowest since August 2010, as the 30-year mortgage rate reached 7.42% (+12bps). Inventory rose +4.6% y/y to 5.1 months supply. The S&P 500 Real Estate Index fell 0.5% on the day, though Data Center REITs bucked the trend at +0.78% (YTD +31.55%).

bullets.title: CSCO beats big on AI infrastructure — raises FY27 revenue $2.5B, AI hyperscaler target to $9B (+100% YoY)
bullets.body: Cisco reported Q1 EPS $1.40 vs $1.33 consensus and revenue $18.52B vs $18.12B, raising FY27 guidance to $74.8-75.8B (from $72.2-73.4B) and EPS to $5.47-5.53 (+8%). AI hyperscaler revenue target raised to $9B in FY27 (12% of total vs 6% in FY26), more than doubling FY26 levels. Stock faded from initial highs as product orders ex-hyperscalers decelerated to 14% and gross margin faces ~200bps headwind from hardware mix; stock -2.8% in premarket.

bullets.title: AMAT beats and raises — 2027 WFE growth guided >30%, Semi Systems to outperform; stocks see PT cuts on multiple compression
bullets.body: Applied Materials reported Q4 EPS $4.16 vs $4.06 consensus and revenue $10.41B vs $10.30B, guiding Q1 to $4.35 EPS (vs $4.24 consensus) and $11.1B revenue (vs $10.85B). Management sees 2027 WFE growing >30% with AMAT outperforming the market, driven by advanced chip demand exceeding supply and customers providing 8-quarter demand forecasts. Multiple banks (GS, Citi, RBC) cut PTs on peer multiple compression (Citi to $580, GS to $580, RBC $600) but maintain Buy ratings.

bullets.title: MSFT global outage — Outlook, Teams, Copilot disrupted; recovery progressing, no malicious activity found
bullets.body: Microsoft suffered a widespread outage impacting Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot globally, with the cause under investigation (mysterious traffic surge, not a cyberattack). Recovery is progressing in phases across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific as of Friday 8am ET. MSFT stock is -1.3% in premarket; cybersecurity names (CRWD +2.3%, ZS +2.3%, NET +1.1%) rallied on spillover demand.

bullets.title: Data center capex boom peaks 2028/2029 — contributing ~2ppts to GDP now, then cooling sharply
bullets.body: PSC Macro warns the data center construction cycle tops out in 2028/2029 after a healthy run through 2027, with tech capex currently contributing ~2ppts to GDP. A steep drop in datacenter announcements/plans threatens construction activity and tech equipment demand in 2028/2029, with negative free cash flows for hyperscalers and neoclouds posing headwinds during the Fed tightening cycle. Near-term demand remains robust, with moratoriums (Texas ~25% of planned capacity) more likely to delay than cancel projects.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples under pressure — IGV -9.5% YTD vs S&P +10.5%; All-SaaS at 5.4x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: The Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.4x FY+2 EV/Sales (All-Security 7.8x, All-Vertical 6.9x), with All-SaaS multiples down 6.24% week-over-week and All-Security down 10.77% week-over-week. IGV has returned -9.5% YTD versus S&P 500 +10.5%. Software Q3 earnings are skewing negative post-results despite several beat-and-raise reports.

bullets.title: OpenAI launches cybersecurity products — direct competitive threat to PANW, CRWD, TENB, QLYS specialists
bullets.body: OpenAI launched 'Daybreak Red Team' and 'Daybreak Defense Factory' products, entering vulnerability management, patching, and pen-testing markets previously served by specialist vendors. Frontier AI labs are now strategically expanding into cybersecurity with potential moves into the AI SOC market, posing an integration-vs-specialization competitive dynamic for PANW and CRWD.

bullets.title: AI inference demand above supply; AVGO flagged as best risk/reward with 37% upside — NVDA at 10.6x FY2 P/E
bullets.body: Wolfe Research sees AI inference demand remaining above industry supply and strengthening into year-end. NVDA is trading at 10.6x FY2 P/E (65% discount to 5-year avg), while AVGO and MRVL are at 12% and 14% discounts to their 5-year averages. Wolfe names AVGO as best risk/reward ($500 PT, 37.2% upside) and MRVL with 128% upside to $375 PT; recent selloff attributed to infrastructure/power fears viewed as temporary and over-discounted.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO (11/19) seen as near-term AI rally catalyst — $1.4-1.5T valuation, $10-15B index demand
bullets.body: The ANT IPO is pricing November 19 at a $1.4-1.5T valuation (down from $1.5-2T earlier), with $10-15B of index tracking demand expected in the first four weeks from Nasdaq/MSCI inclusion. With major negative catalysts (midterms, earnings, rates) largely behind the market, analysts see the IPO as a potential catalyst for an AI sector bounce through mid-December. Risks include 316M shares (38% of float) unlocking day one, potential $20B+ selling pressure if fully exercised.

bullets.title: CBRS beats and surges 13% — raises FY26 guidance, signs MSFT/ORCL cloud deals; PT cuts on valuation
bullets.body: Cerebras reported a beat across all Sep-Q metrics and raised FY26 core revenue guidance to $940-960M with gross margin improving to 42-44%. December quarter guidance of $310-330M (~40% QoQ growth) includes new Oracle hardware orders and a new MSFT cloud deal. Multiple analysts cut price targets on peer multiple normalization (Citi to $250 from $320, 7x EV/S) while maintaining Buy, citing first-mover advantage in fast-inference compute.

bullets.title: Hon Hai bullish on AI rack demand — 'high double-digit' shipment growth q/q and for 2027
bullets.body: Hon Hai (Foxconn) beat Q3 consensus and guided positively for 2027, expecting 'high double-digit growth' in AI rack shipments both quarter-over-quarter and for full year 2027. Cloud & Networking already exceeds 50% of 2026 revenue and is expected to grow beyond 60% over 3-5 years, with no near-term signs of AI demand weakness as orders are already in the pipeline.

bullets.title: HUBS co-founder Halligan returns as CEO — 'refounding' seen as sentiment reset for AI monetization
bullets.body: HubSpot announced Brian Halligan is returning as CEO, replacing Yamini Rangan, in what the company described as a 're-founding' across product, go-to-market, and culture. CTO Duncan Lennox was promoted to President of Product and CFO Kate Bueker will retire February 2027. JPM and Jefferies view the move positively, expecting faster clarity on AI monetization (new seats+credits model) and resolution of expansion rate and net customer add pressures; Q4/FY26 guidance was reaffirmed.

bullets.title: Premarket snapshot: S&P futures +0.31%, 10Y +3bps to 5.15%; VRT +2.1%, AMD -2.5%, CSCO -2.8%
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures are up 23.8 points (+0.31%) to 7,639 in premarket Friday. Vertiv (VRT) leads on a 60% dividend increase (+2.1%); NVDA +1.7% recovering from yesterday's selloff. Laggards include CSCO -2.8% on mixed order metrics post-earnings, AMD -2.5% on earnings, and AVGO -2.2% on a Rothschild/Redburn downgrade. FOXA +2.0% after Morgan Stanley resumed at Overweight/Top Pick with a $90 PT.

bullets.title: GS cuts NVDA PT to $220, flags EMS/power names (VRT, FLEX, JBL) with 44-63% FY28 EPS downside in AI slowdown scenario
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs cut NVDA's PT to $220 from $300 citing CEO transition risk, while maintaining ~80% CY27 EPS growth intact. GS flags greater earnings risk for EMS/power names with high AI infrastructure exposure: VRT, FLEX, and JBL see FY28 EPS down 44%, 63%, and 58% respectively in a 45% AI capex downside scenario. AI/datacenter downside is viewed as largely priced into electronics and test stocks (APH, BDC, TEL, KEYS), with APH and KEYS best positioned via diversification.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit Nov 18-19 at Shenzhen APEC — trade truce extension, EV/battery, C919 supply chain as beneficiary screens
bullets.body: The Trump-Xi summit is scheduled for November 18-19 during APEC in Shenzhen, with the potential to extend the US-China trade truce beyond January 10, 2027. China has already extended a 24% tariff suspension on US imports for two months from November 10. JPMorgan outlines thematic beneficiaries: EV/battery storage if China ODI in US is approved, C919 supply chain on batch engine approvals, and Chinese feed/hog/poultry names if soybeans are added to the tariff cut list.

bullets.title: AI-driven fiber demand strongest in 20+ years — inference workloads shifting from dark to lit services, tier 2/3 markets opening
bullets.body: JPM's fiber infrastructure panel describes the strongest wave of AI-driven fiber demand in over two decades, with AI labs expanding Zayo's dark fiber customer base from ~4 to ~9 hyperscalers. Power constraints on GPU compute are pushing new data center builds into tier 2/3 markets, boosting rural providers. Inference workloads are accelerating a structural shift from dark fiber toward managed lit/wavelength services, with existing routes offering 18-24 month time-to-market vs 3-5 years for greenfield builds.
